themes.title: Far-Right Momentum and Electoral Contestation Ahead of Major Votes
themes.blurb: Far-right and right-wing populist parties across Europe are leveraging high polling numbers and parliamentary leverage to demand executive power or consolidate electoral coalitions. From AfD's record polling in Germany and RN's 2027 platform rollout in France to SD's posturing in Sweden, right-wing movements are framing upcoming elections as decisive turning points against incumbent establishments.

themes.title: National Priority Rhetoric and Hardline Migration Demands
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties across multiple European nations are intensifying demands for aggressive migration curbs, framing foreign populations as economic and social burdens. Promoted policies range from revoking residency permits for unemployed foreigners to curtailing state-funded translation services and attacking multilateral climate agreements.

themes.title: Judicial Crackdowns and Surveillance Targeting the Far-Right
themes.blurb: Key right-wing figures and party allies face escalating judicial scrutiny, criminal investigations, and legal restrictions across several countries. Right-wing factions frame these actions as politically motivated weaponization of the state apparatus, while judicial authorities press forward with probes into trafficking, corruption, and political misconduct.

themes.title: Transnational Right-Wing Networking and Parallel Diplomacy
themes.blurb: Right-wing political movements are increasingly engaging in cross-border diplomacy, bilateral meetings, and international solidarity initiatives outside established diplomatic channels. These actions seek to forge transnational conservative alliances, coordinate strategic messaging, and bypass traditional multilateral institutions.

themes.title: Anti-Establishment Hostility to Public Media and Information Control
themes.blurb: Right-wing leaders across multiple nations are locked in high-profile battles with state broadcasters and digital platforms, accusing traditional media of partisan bias and selective editing. In response, populist politicians are demanding raw video rights or bypassing journalists altogether to stream direct-to-consumer content to their bases.
